back: A crop grown mainly for sale, e.g. cotton and flue-cured tobacco.
Removing the flower head so food goes to the leaves, which become larger and heavier.
Removing side shoots that grow in leaf axils after topping, by hand or with a sucker-control chemical.
Yellowing (about 35 °C, humid), leaf drying (colour fixing), midrib drying (up to about 70 °C).
American bollworm, red bollworm, aphids (sticky lint), jassids, red spider mite.
Stalks uprooted and destroyed after harvest so bollworms have no host; required by regulation in Zimbabwe.
Pick fully open bolls when dry, into cotton bags, keep clean, sort grades, control aphids.
Chloride spoils the burning quality of the leaf; use potassium sulfate, not muriate of potash.
A company supplies inputs on credit and buys the crop, deducting input costs from the payment.
